samples.summary: 'enter over a select-all' never asserts the Enter actually split — only the delete half is pinned
samples.evidence: Lines 406-415 assert only `undoStack.length === before + 1` and that `editor.undo()` restores `original`. Both hold if `handleEnter` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2674) deleted the selection but the subsequent `docSplitBlock` silently no-op'd: the delete alone is one unit and undo restores the same 100 paragraphs. The sibling tests deliberately close this hole (`expect(texts()).toEqual(['X'])` at line 341, `some(b => b.type === 'page-break')` at line 424-426, `toEqual(['Pasted'])` at line 456), and the block comment at 388-398 claims each new test asserts both halves — the Enter case does not. samples.evidence: Grepping `this.deleteSelection()` in packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts shows composite `withUndoUnit` sites the new tests still do not cover: the programmatic `insertText` API path (line 834), Enter inside a table cell (line 2651) and the Hangul commit-over-selection path (line 5882). finding.summary: Enter / page-break / IME-commit / programmatic-paste paths were wrapped in `withUndoUnit` with no test covering their undo cost
finding.evidence: The diff converts five more composite actions to `withUndoUnit`: `handleEnter`'s cell branch (text-editor.ts:2651), its body branch (:2674), `handlePageBreak` (:2714), `pasteAsPlainText` (:4247) and the Hangul commit-over-selection path (:5882). The only editor-level undo-unit assertions added are for typing (`type('X')`), HTML paste, and Backspace (`editor-undo-selection.test.ts:340-388`). Grepping the frontend docs tests for `key: 'Enter'` finds only split/merge repro cases with no `getUndoStackForTest()` counting, and `handlePageBreak`/`pasteAsPlainText` appear in no test file. Pressing Enter over a select-all is exactly the #1045 shape (delete N blocks then split) — if that batch is dropped or the snapshot/batch ordering regresses there, the same >50-entry stack overflow silently destroys the tail of the document, and nothing in the suite notices.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test covers the undo cost of the newly wrapped Enter, page-break and plain-text-paste paths. editor-undo-selection.test.ts contains a dedicated section (over a 100-paragraph document, i.e. above Yorkie's 50-entry cap) that tests exactly these three: 'enter over a select-all is one undo unit' (:406-415), 'a page break over a select-all is one undo unit' (:417-430, which also asserts the page-break block actually landed so the unit is not vacuously empty), and 'a plain-text paste over a select-all is one undo unit' (:432-470). Each asserts getUndoStackForTest().length === before + 1 AND that a single editor.undo() restores all 100 original paragraphs — both halves, count and round-trip. The reviewer's greps missed them because keys are dispatched through a local pressKey(key, init) helper building new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key, ... }) at :399-404, not a literal `key: 'Enter'`, and handlePageBreak/pasteAsPlainText are reached via the keymap rather than by name. Only the Hangul commit-over-selection branch (text-editor.ts:5882) lacks undo-cost coverage; that residual is a contained edge case, not the '#1045 shape destroys the document tail undetected' defect the finding asserts.
